Posterior draws for individual smooths

Source: R/gamm4-methods.R, R/posterior-samples.R
smooth_samples.Rd

Returns draws from the posterior distributions of smooth functions in a GAM. Useful, for example, for visualising the uncertainty in individual estimated functions.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
smooth_samples(model, ...)

smooth_samples(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
smooth_samples(
  model,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  chains = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("gaussian", "mh", "inla", "user"),
  n_cores = 1L,
  n_threads = 1L,
  burnin = 1000,
  thin = 1L,
  t_df = 40,
  rw_scale = 0.25,
  frequentist = FALSE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  draws = NULL,
  diagnostics = FALSE,
  mh_backend = c("mgcv", "gratia", "family"),
  mvn_method = c("mvnfast", "mgcv"),
  block_size = 10000L,
  dense_limit = 5e+06,
  select = NULL,
  n_grid = 200L,
  partial_match = NULL,
  envir = NULL
)

Arguments

model

a fitted model of the supported types; see diagnostic_support.

...

arguments passed to other methods. For fitted_samples(), these are passed on to mgcv::predict.gam(). For posterior_samples() these are passed on to fitted_samples(). For predicted_samples() these are passed on to the relevant simulate() method.

data

data frame; new observations at which the posterior draws from the model should be evaluated. If not supplied, the data used to fit the model will be used for data, if available in model.

n_draws

positive integer; total retained draws across all chains. Required when generating draws. With method = "user", the supplied matrix determines the count; an explicit count must agree with its rows.

chains

positive integer or NULL; number of chains. NULL uses one chain, or the chain mapping in supplied draws. n_draws must be divisible by chains. Burn-in is applied separately to each MH chain.

seed

numeric; a random seed for the simulations.

method

character; which method should be used to draw samples from the posterior distribution. "gaussian" uses a Gaussian (Laplace) approximation to the posterior. "mh" uses a Metropolis Hastings sampler that alternates t proposals with proposals based on a shrunken version of the posterior covariance matrix. "inla" uses a variant of Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation due to Wood (2019), (currently not implemented). "user" allows for user-supplied posterior draws as a coefficient matrix.

n_cores

positive integer; maximum concurrent MH chains using mirai, capped at chains. Existing workers are reused; otherwise temporary workers are created and cleaned up. Only used by method = "mh".

n_threads

positive integer; threads within Gaussian sampling using mvnfast. Defaults to one. This is separate from concurrent MH chains.

burnin

numeric; number of samples to discard as the burnin draws. Only used with method = "mh".

thin

positive integer; retain every thin iterations after burn-in.

t_df

numeric; degrees of freedom for t distribution proposals. Only used with method = "mh".

rw_scale

numeric; Factor by which to scale posterior covariance matrix when generating random walk proposals. Negative or non finite to skip the random walk step. Only used with method = "mh".

frequentist

logical; TRUE to use the frequentist covariance matrix of the parameter estimators, FALSE to use the Bayesian posterior covariance matrix of the parameters.

unconditional

logical; if TRUE (and frequentist == FALSE) then the Bayesian smoothing parameter uncertainty corrected covariance matrix is used, if available.

draws

matrix; user supplied posterior draws to be used when method = "user".

diagnostics

logical; calculate coefficient R-hat, effective sample sizes, and Monte Carlo standard errors using the optional posterior package.

mh_backend

character; "mgcv" preserves mgcv::gam.mh(). "gratia" uses compiled common-family likelihoods. "family" uses a compiled MH loop with callbacks to the fitted family object. Both support independent-observation bam fits. Smoothing parameters and parameters outside the fitted coefficient vector remain fixed. LSS scale and shape coefficients are sampled jointly with location. The family backend caches a full design matrix, smoothing penalty, and proposal factorisation once for all chains.

mvn_method

character; one of "mvnfast" or "mgcv". The default is uses mvnfast::rmvn(), which can be considerably faster at generate large numbers of MVN random values than mgcv::rmvn(), but which might not work for some marginal fits, such as those where the covariance matrix is close to singular.

block_size

positive integer; maximum observation rows per block in the gratia MH evaluator. Large designs are evaluated without storing a full matrix.

dense_limit

numeric; maximum number of design-matrix elements to cache for the gratia MH backend. Use zero to force blockwise evaluation.

select

character; select which smooth's posterior to draw from. The default (NULL) means the posteriors of all smooths in model will be sampled from. If supplied, a character vector of requested terms.

n_grid

positive integer; resolution for constructing evaluation data if data not supplied

partial_match

logical; should smooths be selected by partial matches with select? If TRUE, select can only be a single string to match against.

envir

an optional environment for looking up data, functions and constants. Defaults to the model's evaluation environment.

Value

A tibble with additional classes "smooth_samples" and `"posterior_samples".

For the "gam" method, the columns currently returned (not in this order) are:

  • .smooth; character vector. Indicates the smooth function for that particular draw,

  • .term; character vector. Similar to smooth, but will contain the full label for the smooth, to differentiate factor-by smooths for example.

  • .by; character vector. If the smooth involves a by term, the by variable will be named here, NA_character_ otherwise.

  • .row; integer. A vector of values seq_len(nrow(data)), repeated if n_draws > 1L. Indexes the row in data for that particular draw.

  • .draw; integer. A vector of integer values indexing the particular posterior draw that each row belongs to.

  • .value; numeric. The value of smooth function for this posterior draw and covariate combination.

  • xxx; numeric. A series of one or more columns containing data required for the smooth, named as per the variables involved in the respective smooth.

  • Additional columns will be present in the case of factor by smooths, which will contain the level for the factor named in by_variable for that particular posterior draw.

Details

For LSS models, each smooth is a contribution to its own linear predictor. Select its full smooth label to distinguish predictors, for example s(x) and s.1(x). These are component draws on the predictor scale; use fitted_samples() with quantity = "expectation" for the expected response and derivative_samples() for its derivative. Coefficients are drawn jointly across all predictors.

Warning

The set of variables returned and their order in the tibble is subject to change in future versions. Don't rely on position.

Parallel calculation

With mirai and carrier installed, configure workers with mirai::daemons() to distribute calculations across selected smooths. difference_smooths() distributes factor-level comparisons instead. Without configured workers, or with only one calculation, evaluation is serial. These functions leave the caller's worker pool running.

Model selection, evaluation of model expressions and random draws are prepared in the caller. Workers receive the coordinates and coefficient columns needed for their calculation. Custom prediction methods are evaluated in the caller, including custom tensor margins and factor-smooth bases; workers receive their prediction matrices. Simultaneous intervals use successive draws in selection order, so set.seed() gives the same results with or without workers, independently of their number or completion order. derivatives() uses set.seed(); the other functions also accept seed, which restores the caller's random number state on exit.

smooth_samples() draws coefficients jointly once, then reuses those draws for every smooth, preserving dependence and chain identities. Sampling finishes before smooth calculations start, so MH chains and smooth workers are not nested. Sampling thread controls keep their existing meanings. Workers use their configured BLAS thread settings; when using a threaded BLAS, limit its threads before starting daemons to avoid competing threads.

Parallel work is most useful for expensive bases or interval calculations. Small grids can be slower because of transfer and scheduling costs. Large grids and many draws also require memory for worker inputs and returned results, in addition to the final output.

Author

Gavin L. Simpson

Examples

load_mgcv()
dat <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, seed = 2)
m1 <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = dat, method = "REML")

sms <- smooth_samples(m1, select = "s(x0)", n_draws = 5, seed = 42)
# \donttest{
sms
#> # A tibble: 1,000 x 8
#>    .smooth .term .type .by    .row .draw .value      x0
#>    <chr>   <chr> <chr> <chr> <int> <int>  <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        1     1 -0.357 0.00711
#>  2 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        1     2 -0.465 0.00711
#>  3 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        1     3 -0.720 0.00711
#>  4 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        1     4 -1.27  0.00711
#>  5 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        1     5 -1.18  0.00711
#>  6 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        2     1 -0.365 0.0121 
#>  7 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        2     2 -0.464 0.0121 
#>  8 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        2     3 -0.708 0.0121 
#>  9 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        2     4 -1.24  0.0121 
#> 10 s(x0)   s(x0) TPRS  NA        2     5 -1.16  0.0121 
#> # i 990 more rows
# }

## A factor by example (with a spurious covariate x0)
dat <- data_sim("eg4", n = 1000, seed = 2)

## fit model...
m2 <- gam(y ~ fac + s(x2, by = fac) + s(x0), data = dat)
sms <- smooth_samples(m2, n_draws = 5, seed = 42)
draw(sms)
